vaccines.name: Typhoid
vaccines.description: Typhoid vaccines protect against Salmonella Typhi infection, a cause of severe fever and complications.
considerations: Recommended for HCWs in endemic settings

vaccines.name: Measles
vaccines.description: Measles vaccine protects against a highly contagious viral disease that can be fatal.
considerations: Earlier dose at 6 months in outbreak settings
Safe in HIV-infected infants if not severely immunocompromised

vaccines.name: Mumps
vaccines.description: Mumps vaccine, usually given as part of MMR, prevents viral infection of salivary glands.
considerations: Usually part of MMR combination vaccine

vaccines.name: DTP-containing vaccine (DTPCV)
vaccines.description: Combination vaccine protects against diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis (whooping cough).
considerations: Can be part of combination vaccine

vaccines.name: Japanese Encephalitis (JE)
vaccines.type: Varies by product (inactivated, live attenuated, recombinant)
vaccines.description: JE vaccine protects against Japanese encephalitis, a mosquito-borne viral brain infection.
considerations: Vaccine choice based on availability and national policy

vaccines.name: Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)
vaccines.description: Hib vaccine prevents infections like meningitis and pneumonia caused by Hib bacteria.
considerations: Not recommended after age 5 unless immunocompromised

vaccines.name: Hepatitis A
vaccines.description: Hepatitis A vaccine prevents liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus.
considerations: HCWs in endemic areas or labs handling HAV
Routine use in high endemic areas

vaccines.name: Dengue
vaccines.description: Dengue vaccine helps reduce severe disease and hospitalization in seropositive individuals.
considerations: Not for travelers or HCWs unless in endemic zones

vaccines.name: Polio (bOPV + IPV)
vaccines.description: Polio vaccines protect against poliomyelitis, a disease that can cause paralysis.
considerations: Zero dose (bOPV) at birth in high-risk areas
Use of fractional vs full dose IPV

vaccines.name: Rotavirus
vaccines.description: Rotavirus vaccine prevents diarrheal disease caused by rotavirus in young children.
considerations: Not recommended after 24 months of age

vaccines.name: Rubella
vaccines.description: Rubella vaccine prevents German measles, especially important for preventing congenital rubella syndrome.
considerations: Pregnancy should be avoided for 1 month after vaccination

vaccines.name: Cholera
vaccines.description: Oral cholera vaccines are used to prevent cholera outbreaks in high-risk areas.
considerations: Not part of routine childhood immunization
Used in mass vaccination during outbreaks

vaccines.name: BCG
vaccines.description: BCG vaccine protects against tuberculosis, especially severe forms in children.
considerations: Recommended in HIV+ children if immunologically stable

doses.note: As soon as possible after birth

vaccines.name: Malaria
vaccines.description: Malaria vaccines are used to prevent severe malaria in children in high-transmission areas.

vaccines.name: Seasonal Influenza
vaccines.description: Flu vaccines protect against seasonal influenza viruses and reduce complications in high-risk groups.
considerations: Intranasal only for certain age groups

vaccines.name: Yellow Fever
vaccines.description: Yellow fever vaccine protects against a mosquito-borne viral hemorrhagic disease.
considerations: Avoid during pregnancy unless high risk
Co-administer with measles vaccine if needed

vaccines.name: Meningococcal
vaccines.description: Meningococcal vaccines protect against meningitis caused by Neisseria meningitidis.

vaccines.name: Rabies
vaccines.description: Rabies vaccine is used both before and after exposure to prevent rabies infection.
considerations: Pre-exposure for vets, animal handlers, lab workers

vaccines.name: HPV
vaccines.description: HPV vaccine protects against human papillomavirus infections that cause cervical cancer.
considerations: Off-label single-dose use permitted by WHO

vaccines.name: Pneumococcal (Conjugate)
vaccines.description: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) protects against pneumonia, meningitis, and sepsis.
considerations: Booster important for HIV+ and preterm infants

vaccines.name: Hepatitis B
vaccines.description: Hepatitis B vaccine prevents liver infection and chronic complications caused by hepatitis B virus.
considerations: Recommended in HIV, liver disease, dialysis patients, and health care workers
Essential to prevent perinatal HBV transmission

vaccines.name: Varicella
vaccines.description: Varicella vaccine prevents chickenpox, a common and contagious childhood disease.

vaccines.name: Tick-Borne Encephalitis (TBE)
vaccines.description: TBE vaccine prevents viral brain infection spread by ticks in endemic areas.
considerations: For people living in or traveling to endemic areas
Recommended for laboratory personnel handling TBE virus
